name: Godot 4.7 moved whole sections of the documentation
summary: contributing/development/... became engine_details/development/..., and the GDExtension pages moved under engine_details/engine_api/ — old links 404 rather than redirect.
detail: Written against 4.7.2-stable; docs.godotengine.org/en/stable serves the 4.7 branch. Pages that moved include Optimizing a build for size and Compiling with PCK encryption key (now under engine_details/development/compiling/) and the whole GDExtension section (now engine_details/engine_api/gdextension/). A 4.3 or 4.4 URL for any of these still resolves to the OLD version of the page, which is how stale claims get cited as current. Always check the version banner on a Godot docs page before quoting it.

name: Godot 4 project layout and naming
summary: snake_case for every file and folder, PascalCase for node names and class_name; group by subsystem or content type but never both; .gdignore is an empty file, not a pattern file.
detail: snake_case is not taste: Windows and macOS are case-insensitive while Linux and the exporter are not, so res://Art/Comet.png can resolve locally and fail on a Linux CI export. GDScript has no namespaces, so class_name is a project-wide claim that collides with addons — prefix generic names. An empty .gdignore makes the importer skip a directory and hides it from the FileSystem dock; its contents are ignored.

name: *.uid files must be committed; .godot/ must not
summary: Since Godot 4.4 every resource, script and shader gets a .uid sidecar and references are stored as uid://; not committing them works locally and breaks on a fresh clone.
detail: The official 4.4 announcement is explicit that *.uid should NOT be gitignored. Without them references fall back to path resolution with warnings, and two resources swapping positions is undetectable. Move or delete the .uid alongside any script moved outside the editor. Gitignore .godot/ (which contains export_credentials.cfg, so ignoring the folder covers the secret) and *.translation. Use Project > Version Control > Generate Version Control Metadata — the 3.x/4.0 ignore lists circulating online are wrong for 4.1+ and will commit secrets.

name: Autoloads: four, not forty
summary: Autoloads register under Project Settings > Globals > Autoload, become global identifiers added to root before any scene, and calling free()/queue_free() on one is a documented engine crash.
detail: A script autoload gets a bare Node created for it; a scene autoload is instantiated. List order is load order. The failure mode of over-using them is a project where every subsystem reaches every other and nothing can be exercised in isolation — exactly what Cosmo's typed host/scene boundary exists to prevent. For the rebuild: save store, music scheduler, run state, settings/telemetry. Everything else is a node in the scene it belongs to.

name: Authored tables become custom Resources; tuned scalars stay const
summary: Rings, worlds, orb pools, formation tiers and level windows want class_name X extends Resource with @export and typed Array[T]; a playtested number wants a const in a .gd, because .tres cannot hold its comment.
detail: Typed Array[OrbSpec] gives an inspector drag-target that rejects the wrong type; untyped Array does not. Resources are cached and SHARED — two scenes loading the same .tres get the same object, so treat specs as immutable or duplicate() explicitly. Never load() a resource from a player or server: a .tres names a script path and FileAccess.get_var(true) deserialises objects that can execute code. The const-vs-Resource split maps onto the database's own spec-vs-tuning distinction.

name: Feature-tag overrides, and the get_setting trap
summary: project.godot supports per-platform overrides with a suffix (renderer/rendering_method.web); ProjectSettings.get_setting() ignores them and returns the base value — only get_setting_with_override() respects them.
detail: This fails silently: the value returned is a value, just the wrong one, and the symptom is behaviour differing between editor and export for no visible reason. Default tags cover platforms (android/ios/web/windows/macos/linuxbsd), build types (debug/release/editor/template), architectures (arm64/wasm32/...), device classes (mobile/pc/web) and threads/nothreads. Custom feature tags are declared per export preset and do NOT apply when running from the editor, by design.

name: Portrait mobile project settings
summary: stretch/mode canvas_items with stretch/aspect expand and handheld/orientation portrait; the docs' mobile example is 720x1280 with 1080x1920 offered for high-end devices.
detail: canvas_items renders at device resolution and scales the 2D coordinate system, keeping text and shader output crisp; viewport renders at the base size and blits, avoiding scaling artifacts but discarding resolution. expand grows the viewport in the long axis rather than letterboxing, which is what makes a 19.5:9 phone usable — and which means the visible height is NOT fixed. Any rebuild that hard-codes 1920 will look wrong on a 20:9 phone. Cosmo already lives under this constraint in Phaser.

name: Export presets, secrets and the CI command line
summary: Commit export_presets.cfg; never commit .godot/export_credentials.cfg. CI runs godot --headless --import first, then --export-release "<preset>" <path>.
detail: --headless is required on a runner with no GPU. --import 'starts the editor, waits for any resources to be imported, and then quits'; on a clean checkout with no .godot/ cache, skipping it ships a pack with unimported assets and no error you notice. Five resource export modes plus an include filter for non-resources (*.json, *.txt, *.csv) and an exclude filter — Godot's version of a publish allowlist, and weaker than Cosmo's, which fails the build rather than relying on a glob you remembered to write.

name: Reproducing a build stamp without a bundler define
summary: Godot has no Vite-style define; generate game/build_stamp.gd from git in CI before exporting, or use an EditorExportPlugin._export_begin() with add_file().
detail: The generated-file route is deterministic and needs no editor plugin — keep a checked-in placeholder so the editor always parses. The EditorExportPlugin route stamps manual editor exports too, at the cost of a git subprocess inside the export path that fails on a machine without git on PATH. Either way the invariant is unchanged: a build stamp identifies source, never deployment. docs/invariants.md still governs.

name: Custom export templates and what they actually cost
summary: Build profiles, disable_3d=yes (~15% for 2D), optimize=size or size_extra (4.5+), lto=full (12-16 GB RAM) and stripping (5-10x) shrink the binary — at the price of a toolchain per platform, forever.
detail: The build-profile route (scons build_profile=/path/to/profile.gdbuild) has the highest leverage: the editor detects which engine features the project touches. The docs warn detection 'may occasionally be too aggressive', so a custom-template build can run in the editor and crash on a stripped feature — verify by playing it. 4.7 added downloading only the platforms you need, which helps CI cache size. Optional ICU Data is a separate download and is what buys CJK/Thai and emoji.

name: What the Godot web export requires
summary: WebAssembly and WebGL 2.0 via the Compatibility renderer only; single-threaded is the default since 4.3, and Thread Support or Extensions Support both require COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp headers.
detail: Those two headers gate SharedArrayBuffer and, once set, stop the page freely embedding or calling other origins — the thing that broke Godot games on itch.io. Progressive Web App > Enable installs a service-worker workaround that simulates the headers when you cannot set them on the host. Forward+ and Mobile renderers do not export to web at all. The export cannot be opened over file://; it needs a server, the same constraint CLAUDE.md already states for the Vite entry.

name: The web export's initial download, measured against Cosmo's
summary: Godot 4.3's engine .wasm was ~40 MB uncompressed and ~5 MB Brotli; Cosmo's entire current first load is 439,055 B of gzipped JS plus 788,521 B of WebP. Assume a 5-10x regression.
detail: The 4.3 figures are the only official ones published; 4.7's are not, and were not measured here — treat ~5 MB Brotli as an order of magnitude, not a promise. Measured in this checkout on 2026-09-07: dist/ is 4,004,830 B across 47 files, dist/assets/index-DG2O-aGv.js is 1,621,182 B (439,055 B gzipped), public/art/ is 788,521 B across 25 files. Serve .wasm as application/wasm and precompress; GitHub Pages gzips automatically, itch.io does not, GitLab Pages needs manual precompression, Netlify does Brotli — so the Pages copy will be heavier than the Netlify one.

name: Web audio: Sample mode has no AudioEffects, Stream mode has latency
summary: Web exports default to Sample playback, where AudioEffects are not supported; Stream playback restores them but 'incurs increased latency if threads are not enabled', and threads need cross-origin isolation.
detail: AudioServer.PLAYBACK_TYPE_SAMPLE is documented as 'Only currently supported on the web platform. AudioEffects are not supported when playback is considered as a sample.' The default is set by audio/general/default_playback_type and its .web override, and per node by AudioStreamPlayer.playback_type — which is itself marked experimental and 'may be changed or removed in future versions'. This is the single hardest constraint the web export puts on Cosmo, whose music is a scheduled synthesis chain with a bus and a measured make-up gain.

name: JavaScriptBridge.pwa_update() is a better freshCheck
summary: With PWA enabled the service worker reports a pending version through the pwa_update_available signal and pwa_needs_update(); pwa_update() applies it and reloads the app in every open tab.
detail: This maps one-to-one onto Cosmo's freshCheck() design and its guards — never swap during a live run, only from the menu — with the browser doing the detection instead of a range request over the game's own bundle plus a regex for a BUILD literal. The existing parser is doubly inert in the shipped Phaser build: externalLoop returns early, and minification destroys the const BUILD='…' form it matches anyway. PWA export options also give an Offline Page, icon sizes 144/180/512, orientation, display mode, and the cross-origin isolation header workaround.

name: What an iPhone player actually gets from the web export
summary: Godot's docs recommend Chromium or Firefox because 'Safari has several issues with WebGL 2.0 support' — advice unavailable on iOS, where every browser is Safari's engine.
detail: The one piece of good news is that the single-threaded export 'works very well on macOS and iOS too, where it always had compatibility issues with multiple threads exports'. Concretely an iPhone player gets: a multi-megabyte download; the WebGL 2.0 path Godot's own docs consider weakest; audio that will not start until they touch the screen; the game pausing whenever the tab is backgrounded because _process() stops; and no reliable fullscreen without an input event. The native iOS app stops being a nice-to-have after this move.

name: user:// across platforms, and why the project name is load-bearing
summary: user:// is %APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/<project> on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/... on macOS, ~/.local/share/godot/... on Linux, app-private on mobile, and an IndexedDB virtual filesystem on web.
detail: res:// is not writable in an exported project; only user:// is documented as guaranteed writable. The path derives from the project NAME, so renaming the project orphans every save — set application/config/use_custom_user_dir and a stable custom_user_dir_name on day one. This is the exact analogue of Cosmo's existing rule that the Capacitor scheme must not change because localStorage is origin-scoped. On web, FileAccess writes sync to IndexedDB automatically; force_fs_sync() exists only for modules that cannot use FileAccess. IndexedDB is site data, so a cleared browser or a private window has no save.

name: ConfigFile or JSON for saves, never store_var
summary: ConfigFile gives load/save/parse plus encrypted variants; its documented trap is that section and property names cannot contain spaces — anything after a space is dropped on save and on load.
detail: FileAccess.store_var/get_var is not a save format: get_var(allow_objects=true) deserialises objects that 'can contain code which gets executed'. Godot does not write atomically either — an interrupted cfg.save(PATH) leaves a truncated file — so write to PATH + '.tmp' and rename through DirAccess. That pattern should hold on web too, since the rename goes through the same virtual filesystem, but the IndexedDB-backed FS is the least-exercised path here and is worth verifying rather than assuming.

name: Encrypted saves: two mechanisms, and why Cosmo wants neither
summary: FileAccess.open_encrypted_with_pass() needs no custom templates; PCK encryption needs SCRIPT_AES256_ENCRYPTION_KEY at engine compile time and 'will not work if you use official, precompiled export templates'.
detail: FileAccess.open_encrypted takes a 32-byte key; open_encrypted_with_pass derives one from a string; ConfigFile.save_encrypted_pass/load_encrypted_pass are the same idea one level up. The PCK route's own docs concede 'the key needs to be stored in the binary', so extraction is harder, not impossible. For Cosmo the whole game is already delivered to the browser and the repository is public; an encrypted local save adds a key you must never lose, breaks a player's ability to recover their own file, and buys nothing. The design already reached the right answer: server-side monotonic merge, which makes a forged best:0 a no-op.

name: JavaScriptBridge is registered on every platform, stubbed off-web
summary: platform/web/api/api.cpp guards its bodies with #if !defined(WEB_ENABLED) and platform/SCsub compiles every platform's api/*.cpp into every build, so JavaScriptBridge.eval() compiles everywhere and returns null off-web.
detail: That makes a same-origin localStorage read safe to write once and guard with OS.has_feature("web"), with no conditional compilation and no Engine.get_singleton() dance. eval(code, use_global_execution_context) runs in the page's window, so any key the previous build wrote to that origin is readable. Verified by reading the 4.7 source, not inferred from the class reference, which only says the singleton is web-only.

name: Native lifecycle and haptics without a WebView bridge
summary: NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED/RESUMED (Android and iOS), FOCUS_IN/FOCUS_OUT, WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST and set_auto_accept_quit(false) replace the whole Capacitor bridge; Input.vibrate_handheld is far blunter than @capacitor/haptics.
detail: MainLoop defines APPLICATION_RESUMED=2014, APPLICATION_PAUSED=2015, APPLICATION_FOCUS_IN=2016, APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT=2017 and OS_MEMORY_WARNING=2009 (iOS). WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST fires on Android Back while Application > Config > Quit On Go Back is enabled, which is the default. Input.vibrate_handheld(duration_ms:int=500, amplitude:float=-1.0) is one blunt pulse — Cosmo's six haptic kinds, its 65 ms rate limit and its priority ordering all have to be rebuilt in GDScript over that primitive.

name: Addons are vendored source with no lockfile
summary: An addon is a folder under res://addons/ with a plugin.cfg, enabled in Project Settings > Plugins; there is no dependency resolution, so commit the source and record the version and commit it came from.
detail: Godot 4.7 replaced the AssetLib browser with an Asset Store, which is a discovery surface, not a package manager. Two risks specific to this project: an addon that claims a class_name you also want, and an editor plugin that writes to project.godot on enable — read the diff the first time. For a one-owner project the correct addon count is close to zero: the tooling has to stay small, and every addon breaks on the next minor engine release and only you can fix it. Provenance goes in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt the way the art already does.

name: Localisation structure, and the decision to make now
summary: CSV imports to .translation, registered under Project Settings > Localization > Translations, read with tr() and tr_n(), with a Remaps tab that swaps whole resources per locale.
detail: The structural decision is not the pipeline, it is not scattering literal strings through the code: writing tr(&"LESSON_FIRST_HOP") costs nothing today and makes the teaching copy addressable. Cosmo has 103 lesson records; retrofitting keys onto them later is the expensive version. The real cost of ever shipping a locale is glyph coverage — the optional ICU Data export-template download is what buys CJK and Thai. Budget the font, not the CSV.

name: GDExtension: the real cost and the five signs that justify it
summary: One compiled artifact per platform and architecture, forced cross-origin isolation on web, godot-cpp pinned to an engine API version, and native stacks instead of GDScript ones.
detail: Justified only when: the profiler shows SCRIPT time dominating a frame missing 16.6 ms on the target device; the hot path is a tight numeric loop over thousands of elements that is not expressible as a shader, MultiMesh or a servers call; per-frame allocation is already gone; everything is already statically typed; or you need a native library with no GDScript equivalent. Cosmo hits none — the heaviest work is shader work on the GPU, the simulation is dozens of entities, and the scheduler's difficulty is timing, not throughput. Reach for RenderingServer and MultiMeshInstance2D first.

name: Godot 3 idiom that fills search results and is wrong in 4.7
summary: yield->await, export var->@export, setget->property setters, the Tween node->create_tween(), the old connect signature->signal.connect(), File/Directory->FileAccess/DirAccess, JavaScript->JavaScriptBridge.
detail: Also: KinematicBody2D->CharacterBody2D, OS.get_screen_size and friends->DisplayServer.*, the tool keyword->@tool. Godot 4-specific traps on the same ground: get_setting() ignoring feature overrides; uncommitted *.uid; committed .godot/ leaking keystore passwords; skipping --import in CI; assuming file:// works; assuming AudioEffects work on web; assuming PCK encryption works with official templates; renaming the project and orphaning every save; free()ing an autoload; and 4.7's moved doc URLs 404ing rather than redirecting.

name: Serve the Godot web build from the existing play origins
summary: Signed-out web players keep their cometloop: records only if the Godot build is served from the same origins; a new subdomain silently loses every one of them.
problem: Every signed-out web player's best score, level reached, run count and lesson flags live in localStorage under a cometloop: prefix, scoped to https://cosmo-arcade.netlify.app and https://ats314.github.io. A Godot web export can read them through JavaScriptBridge.eval, but only from the same origin. Nothing in the repository currently records the play URL as a save-migration constraint — it reads as a link.
proposal: Commit to serving the Godot build from the existing Netlify and Pages origins. Ship a LegacyImport that reads the twelve keys the game actually reads (best, gl, runs, intro, muted, swipe, groove, hopped, landed, struggle, seen, seen2), folds them into user://records.cfg with the same max semantics so a late read cannot lower a record, and writes a migrated_v1 flag. Do not delete the localStorage keys — they are the only copy if the build has to be rolled back. If a new origin is unavoidable, ship a one-time handover page on the old origin instead.
risk: Reading the wrong key names, or folding with replace instead of max, silently lowers a record. The keys cometloop:level and cometloop:mode must stay unread — a stored 7 reads back as level 7 of 6.

name: Prompt sign-in in the current build, before the Godot one exists
summary: Native Capacitor WebView records cannot be read by a Godot native export; the cloud account is the only path that carries them, and the prompt has to ship in the Phaser build to work.
problem: Capacitor stores localStorage inside the WebView's own origin storage (https://localhost on Android, capacitor://localhost on iOS). A Godot native export has no WebView: on Android the data is in a LevelDB the engine cannot read, on iOS inside the app container's WebKit storage. Recovering it would need a platform plugin whose only job is reading a browser database. A signed-out native player's best score does not survive the move, and no work done after the migration can change that.
proposal: Ship a sign-in invitation in the current Phaser build — at the title screen, non-blocking, honouring the existing rule that accounts are optional in the same sense the sound is optional. Every player who signs in before the switch converts from unrecoverable to recoverable, because the server already holds the merged records and the Godot client will call the same /api/progress with the same bearer shape. State the loss plainly in the release notes rather than discovering it in a support message.
risk: A prompt that reads as a demand breaks the optional-account rule and the frictionless title screen. It must never block a local run, and it must not appear mid-run.

name: Settle the web Sample-vs-Stream decision before writing the scheduler
summary: Sample playback (the web default) supports no AudioEffects; Stream playback adds latency without threads, and threads force cross-origin isolation. The scheduler's architecture differs between the two.
problem: Cosmo's music is a scheduled synthesis chain behind a bus with a measured make-up gain, and its hardest requirement is that a drop lands on the beat the player earned. Godot's web export defaults to Sample playback, where AudioServer documents that AudioEffects are not supported. Stream playback restores them but 'incurs increased latency if threads are not enabled', and Thread Support requires COOP/COEP headers that also stop the page embedding or calling other origins. Writing the scheduler before choosing leaves it built against the wrong constraint.
proposal: Pick one before any scheduler code exists. The likely answer is bake, not process: resolve the effects chain into the samples ahead of time so Sample mode is viable and the latency question disappears, leaving only scheduling. If bus effects turn out to be non-negotiable, accept Stream mode plus Thread Support plus COOP/COEP on both hosts and record that the game can then never be embedded in a non-isolated page. Prototype both against a real mid-range phone browser rather than deciding on paper.
risk: Baking removes the ability to change the chain at runtime, which some layer-unlock effects may depend on. Choosing Stream+threads forecloses embedding and adds the cross-origin isolation maintenance burden to both hosts.

name: Let the PWA service worker be the freshness contract
summary: pwa_update_available / pwa_needs_update() / pwa_update() give Cosmo the freshness check it designed, tested and then had to disable — with the browser doing the detection.
problem: freshCheck() is a carefully guarded feature that is inert in the shipped Phaser build twice over: externalLoop returns early at the first statement, and its parser /const BUILD='([0-9a-f]{7})'/ cannot match a minified module bundle even if it ran. smoke.mjs asserts it green because the VM harness builds the runtime with host = {}. A session reading the harness would conclude the play link self-heals; it does not.
proposal: Enable Progressive Web App on the Godot web export and connect JavaScriptBridge.pwa_update_available. Keep both original guards: never swap during a live run, only offer the update at the title screen. Retire the range-request-and-regex approach entirely rather than porting it. Note that pwa_update() reloads the app in ALL open browser tabs, which the old design never did — decide whether that is acceptable or whether the offer should be explicit.
risk: Enabling PWA also enables offline caching and the cross-origin isolation header workaround; a stale service worker is its own class of 'the fix is deployed but the player has the old build'. The offline page needs authoring.

name: Keep the publish allowlist as a CI walk of the export directory
summary: Godot's export filters are a glob you must remember to write; check.mjs is a deny-then-allow pair that fails the build. The check should survive the engine change, not the filters.
problem: tools/check.mjs:489-494 enforces internalAsset (always rejected) and publicAsset (the only things allowed through) over both public/ and dist/, plus a completeness half requiring every public/ file to reach dist/, plus a symlink rejection. Godot offers a non-resource include filter and an exclude filter and nothing that fails a build. Migrating to Godot without porting the check silently drops the guarantee that no internal file becomes a public URL.
proposal: Write the equivalent as a small CI script that walks the exported web directory after godot --export-release. The web export's artifact is a short enumerable set — index.html, .js, .wasm, .pck, the boot-splash .png, plus the PWA service worker, manifest, icons and offline page — so the allowlist gets simpler, not harder. Add the two license assertions that Godot will not do for you: LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt must ship, and the proprietary notice must survive into the exported HTML shell.
risk: An allowlist written against the current export's file set will reject a legitimate new file (a new icon size, a second pack) and block a release until someone widens it. That is the intended failure direction, but it needs to be documented so it is not disabled under time pressure.

name: Generate build_stamp.gd from git before the export
summary: Godot has no Vite-style define, so the commit stamp has to be a generated file written by CI before godot --export-release, with a checked-in placeholder so the editor always parses.
problem: __COSMO_BUILD__ is a Vite define resolved from git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD, falling back to COMMIT_REF then GITHUB_SHA then 'dev'. It is what lets a release check say this page is that commit, and it has no direct equivalent in Godot's build. Without a deliberate replacement the Godot build ships with no way to identify its source, which retires a working piece of release discipline for no reason.
proposal: Write game/build_stamp.gd from CI immediately before the export, carrying the short SHA and an ISO timestamp, with a committed placeholder so the editor and a local run always parse. Expose it the way COSMO_BUILD is exposed today: a faint title-screen line, never drawn during play, plus whatever the Godot equivalent of runtimeSnapshot() becomes. Prefer this over an EditorExportPlugin, which puts a git subprocess inside the export path and fails on a machine without git on PATH.
risk: A generated file that is also committed will produce noisy diffs unless the placeholder is stable and CI's write is not committed back. The invariant that a stamp identifies source and not deployment must be restated, or a stamped build will again be mistaken for a live one.

name: Fix use_custom_user_dir and custom_user_dir_name on day one
summary: user:// is derived from the project name, so a later rename orphans every save — the same failure Cosmo already guards against by freezing the Capacitor schemes.
problem: Godot's default user:// path is %APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/<project_name> and its platform equivalents. The project name is a field people edit. Cosmo already learned this shape of lesson once: capacitor.config.ts freezes server.androidScheme and server.iosScheme because local records and the stored account key are scoped to the WebView origin, and changing a scheme signs every native player out. Nothing in a fresh Godot project prevents the same mistake with the project name.
proposal: Set application/config/use_custom_user_dir = true and application/config/custom_user_dir_name to a fixed string in the first commit that creates the project, and add a line to docs/invariants.md making it a rule with the reason attached — the same way the Capacitor origins are a rule. Verify OS.get_user_data_dir() in a smoke check so a silent change is caught.
risk: Changing it later is the very failure being prevented, so this has to land before any player has a save. Setting it after a beta strands the beta's records.

name: Measure the Godot web payload before committing to official templates
summary: The only published figures are 4.3's ~40 MB wasm / ~5 MB Brotli against Cosmo's current 439 KB gzipped JS; 4.7's numbers are unpublished and unmeasured, and the answer decides whether custom templates are mandatory.
problem: The web export's initial download is the single largest regression this engine change causes, and the size of it is currently a guess. Custom export templates (build profiles, disable_3d, optimize=size_extra, lto=full, stripping) can cut it materially but cost a per-platform toolchain maintained forever by one owner — a cost worth paying only if the official-template number is actually unacceptable.
proposal: Before any content is built, export a hello-world Godot 4.7.2 web build with the intended renderer and thread settings, serve it Brotli-compressed the way Netlify will, and measure the real transfer size and time-to-first-frame on a mid-range phone over cellular. Record the number here. Only then decide whether custom templates are mandatory, and design the loading experience around the number you measured rather than the one you hoped for.
risk: Measuring a hello-world understates the real payload, which also carries the pack, the sky shader and the sprite set. The measurement is a floor, and should be recorded as one.
